notes: GPT-4 rewrote institutional heart failure education materials for readability; no patient-posed questions or lay users and no safety rating of advice responses. Bench; no unsafe tier.

Bench simulated-patient study, ChatGPT, 27 LMIC primary-care trials. Radiation oncology patient care questions; specialty-only. LLM responses rated for accuracy/completeness/conciseness with 2 potentially harmful responses noted, but specialty scope excludes first (FT-R5 before outcome codes).

Community Learning Ledgers paper: framework/architecture and governance proposal for cancer navigation with an embedded benchmark (210 responses, 5 systems, 42 queries; no clinically harmful recommendations reported), not a primary bench evaluation report of patient-facing chatbot advice; also includes a provider clinical-decision-support cohort.

Bench; GPT-4o identified 20 medications from pictures and gave patient education, scored on a 4-point accuracy/precision/clarity scale by the two authors. Medication questions are primary-care relevant; narrative only. Total 20 medication items.
Long-term opioid therapy patient FAQs (13 questions, ChatGPT) scored only for reliability, accuracy and comprehensibility; no explicit unsafe/harmful tier and no secondary outcome in poolable form.

Lay-rescuer prehospital BLS/PALS in-silico cases (ChatGPT/GPT-4): outcomes are diagnostic accuracy and correct/incorrect first-aid items (e.g. ALS techniques incorrectly advised in 3/22 cases); no explicit unsafe tier with numerator/denominator and no poolable secondary outcome. Retained report for the duplicate pair (see R2812).

LLM-assisted post-discharge tuberculosis care: clinician-facing generation of medication counselling, patient education and follow-up plans compared with physicians; errors counted as items (137 LLM vs 36 physician), not patient-posed questions rated for safety. No poolable outcome.
ChatGPT self-diagnosis in common orthopedic diseases: diagnostic accuracy only; no safety tier and no poolable secondary outcome.
Remote orthopedic consultations: ChatGPT-4 vs DingXiangYuan forum physicians scored for quality/dependability on Likert-type scales; no explicit unsafe tier and no poolable secondary outcome.

Perinatal depression FAQs across LLMs scored for reliability/readability with qualitative safety signalling only; no explicit unsafe tier counts and no poolable secondary outcome. Non-crisis mental-health topic, so not FT-R5.
Frequently asked questions in anaesthesia (10 FAQs; ChatGPT-4, Bard, Bing Chat) rated by anaesthesia programme directors; specialty-only perioperative topic set.
Duplicate report of R2769 (same Bushuven et al. BLS/PALS lay-rescuer study; Research Square preprint of the Journal of Medical Systems article). Retained record: R2769.

Anti-LGBTQIA+ bias evaluation (38 expert-designed prompts incl. synthetic clinical notes, 4 LLMs): outcome is bias/inappropriateness, not a clinician-rated unsafe tier for patient advice; no poolable primary or secondary outcome.

GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy questions, LLM vs internet search, graded on 5-point Likert scales including a safety dimension (mean scores only); no explicit unsafe tier counts and no poolable secondary outcome.

Pediatric fever management, 30 questions x 4 models (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, YouChat, Perplexity), rated by doctors and parents on dimension scores; responses deemed safety risks were removed and scored zero for the parent survey but their count is not reported. No poolable outcome. Bench.

Heart failure questions, 107 questions entered twice into GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, graded for accuracy/appropriateness (comprehensive to completely incorrect); no explicit unsafe tier and no poolable secondary outcome.

Laboratory test result interpretation for lay patients, 53 questions, 5 LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, LLaMA 2, MedAlpaca, ORCA_mini); safety assessed as comparative win rates and expert Likert ratings on 7 questions, no unsafe tier counts. No poolable outcome.

Bench. Models ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, DeepSeek, Doubao; 58 public-facing vegetarian/vegan nutrition questions x 5 models = 290 responses, 5 blinded clinically trained raters, safety coded binary safe vs potentially unsafe by majority. PRIMARY: potentially unsafe (labelled potentially harmful in text) 47/290 total, stated in Results/Discussion qualitative safety review; per-model safe/unsafe percentages in Figure 2, exact per-arm counts to confirm from figure/supplement at extraction. Stratum bench.

Bench. Acute appendicitis patient-style questions, 30 questions x 3 systems (ChatGPT GPT-5.2 Instant, Gemini 3 Flash, Microsoft Copilot) x 2 prompting conditions x 3 repeats = 540 responses, rated by 3 blinded surgeons. Explicit major-harm tier (H_any / H_maj) reported only as percentages by question category in the retrieved publisher text (medication H_any 28.8% / H_maj 23.8%; symptom interpretation 19.4% / 16.8%; waiting at home 15.9% / 13.5%; abstract and Methods/Results of saved text); no numerator printed in retrieved text, so nothing poolable. Narrative; flag for coordinator to check VoR tables for counts.

Bench. Sexual health (primary-care relevant), 120 standardised questions x 3 chatbots = 360 responses (ChatGPT-4, Bard, Bing Chat), rated by 2 sexual health clinicians, safety tier safe / minor inaccuracy / potentially harmful (Table 2, Results). Potentially harmful reported only as percentages per arm (ChatGPT-4 7.1%, Bard 9.3%, Bing Chat 11.5% of 120 each), which do not back-convert to integer counts, so no poolable numerator. Narrative.

Online ear, nose and throat inquiries, ChatGPT vs physicians, rated on Likert criteria including absence of harmful content (mean scores only); no explicit unsafe tier counts and no poolable secondary outcome.

Melanoma patient questions, LLM vs patient information resources (Br J Dermatol). Routes tried: Europe PMC search + fullTextXML (no PMCID, 500 error), OpenAlex/Unpaywall OA PDF at Oxford Academic (connection closed / 403). Subscription article; no legitimate full text retrieved.

Bench. Postoperative pain education, 51 questions x 7 interfaces = 357 responses (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, Doubao, Perplexity, Claude), blinded clinical review, binary Safe/Unsafe with Unsafe only for actionable statements plausibly causing clinically important harm. PRIMARY: Unsafe 11/357 total (3.08%), Results abstract and safety section. Per-arm unsafe derived from printed safe-response rates per 51: ChatGPT 1/51, Gemini 0/51, Copilot 1/51, DeepSeek 3/51, Doubao 2/51, Perplexity 2/51, Claude 2/51 (sums to 11; flag derived, verify against Supplementary Table S4 at extraction). Stratum bench.

Bench. Osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture patient-facing questions, 36 questions x 4 chatbots (round 1). Binary safety (0 safe, 1 potentially unsafe), blinded raters. PRIMARY per arm as printed in abstract/Results: ChatGPT 3/36 (8.3%), DeepSeek 5/36 (13.9%), Gemini 6/36 (16.7%), Doubao 7/36 (19.4%); total 21/144. A second generation round (further 144 responses) was for stability analysis. Stratum bench.

Bench. Ramadan medication management for diabetes, 23 prompts x 3 chatbots x 2 languages (English/Arabic) x 2 days = 276 responses. No pure primary unsafe tier: the printed count is an accuracy-scale tier (score 0 = contradicts IDF-DAR guideline OR clinically harmful). SECONDARY (problematic): 30/276 (11%) guideline-conflicting/clinically unsafe responses, Results section and Figure 1; Arabic 14% vs English 8% as printed. A separate 0-3 safety scale is reported only as medians. Primary pool: no. Stratum bench.
Common radiology-related questions in Chinese, online radiologists vs LLM chatbots; specialty-only radiology/imaging question set.

Human-user/bench hybrid. 34 lay participants prompted 4 LLMs with 212 real or imagined health concerns (Gemini-1.5 Pro 140, ChatGPT-3.5 40, ChatGPT-4o 26, Llama3-8B 6); 9 board-certified physicians rated validity, quality of information, understanding/reasoning and Harm on scales (harmful defined as Harm score >=3) but no count of harmful responses is printed in the retrieved text (means and validity/QoI/UaR percentages only). Eligible general primary-care concerns; nothing poolable. Narrative.
Real-world patient medical and administrative queries in nuclear medicine; specialty-only. Expert table reports Harm grades for 76 queries but topic scope excludes first.

STELLA: a safety-testing engine/platform description (framework/tool paper) using simulated users across health scenarios including mental-health crisis content; not a primary evaluation report of patient-facing chatbot advice with rated responses for this review.
Patient questions following cataract surgery; specialty-only postoperative ophthalmology topic.
Cancer-Myth: oncology patient questions with false presuppositions (585 questions); specialty-only cancer topic, paragraph-level harmful labels notwithstanding.

Human-user randomised experiment, 49 lay participants making domestic medical triage decisions on symptom vignettes before/after consulting an LLM conversational agent (rational vs empathic persona). Outcomes are participants' triage accuracy/confidence change; LLM responses were not clinician-rated for safety and no undertriage count for responses is reported. Eligible human-user stratum; nothing poolable. Narrative.

Proof-of-concept for patient use of LLMs with open notes (explaining/summarising patients' own clinical notes); a note-summarisation task, not advice to patient-posed primary-care questions, and no safety rating of advice responses.
Nutritional advice comparison of AI chatbots scored for accuracy, completeness, reproducibility and consistency; no explicit unsafe tier and no poolable secondary outcome.

Women's Health Benchmark: 96 expert model stumps across five specialties and three query types (patient, clinician, evidence/policy), 13 LLMs, outcome is overall error/failure types (~60% failure); no explicit unsafe tier for patient-facing responses separable in poolable form.
Post-treatment quality-of-life questions in head and neck cancer, LLMs vs professional resources; specialty-only oncology topic.
